title: Cache remote reads outside React state with explicit TTL, eviction, and refresh bypass
statement: Hold remote-read caches outside React state: a module-level TTL map with a clear function wired to the Refresh action, a ref-held LRU (Map insertion order) with TTL and size cap, and an in-flight Set that dedupes concurrent fetches.

title: Guard cached freshness against backward clock skew
statement: Treating a negative elapsed delta as ZERO pinned stale content forever; match the error arm of the duration computation and refetch instead.

title: Probe a subprocess without holding the lock, cache the probe
statement: Probe CLI binaries without holding the shared lock, cache the result, and take the version from the first line containing a digit — CLIs print update notices first.

title: Precompute SVG geometry per size in a module cache and memoize the leaf
statement: Precompute path strings and trig once per size in a module-scoped cache (Map<size,Geometry>) and memoize the leaf component, so hover re-renders never rebuild paths; the memo is only effective because the parent keeps handlers stable via useCallback.

title: Cache at the api seam with self-healing on rejection
statement: Module-level caching at the api seam — a TTL promise cache and an HMR-surviving globalThis singleton — must self-heal on rejection: promise.catch clears the slot only if it still owns it, failures reset for retry while successes cache for page lifetime, and the invalidate function is chained onto the mutation's own success. Fire-and-forget telemetry is typed void so no caller can await it.

title: Cap a TTL cache's entry count — TTL gates freshness, not retention
statement: A stale-while-revalidate cache needs a hard size cap with insertion-order eviction on top of its TTL: TTL only decides when data is stale, never when memory is released, so variadic keys (per-entity ids) grow forever in a long-lived session. Re-set a key on write so Map insertion order approximates LRU.

title: Single-flight an expensive probe cache by holding the lock across the recompute
statement: Releasing a cache lock between the miss and the refill lets N concurrent callers all run the expensive work (subprocess fan-outs, cookie-DB copies). Hold the async mutex through the probe so late callers block briefly and then read the first caller's fresh result.

title: Persist the first successful AI derivation as a recipe shared by every entry path
statement: When several UX paths need the same expensive AI-derived artifact (a connector's credential schema), persist the first successful derivation as a named recipe with a memory-cache front so later sessions skip discovery entirely — and treat recipe-cache failures as non-fatal, since caching is an optimization, not a requirement.

title: Both sides of a fingerprint check must call one canonical hash function
statement: When cache reuse depends on a config fingerprint, the write site and the read site must share ONE exported hash helper over the same inputs. If each side hand-rolls a hash over slightly different inputs, the comparison never matches and the cache is a silent permanent no-op — everything cold-starts while looking healthy.

title: Deps imported only by lazy routes must be pre-bundled in dev, or first navigation 504s
statement: With dev-server dependency pre-bundling (Vite optimizeDeps), a package imported exclusively from a lazily-loaded route is first discovered when the user navigates there; the server kicks off a re-optimization mid-session and the in-flight dynamic import fails ('Outdated Optimize Dep' 504). List such deps in the explicit include set so they join the initial optimize pass.

title: A parser cache of size one shared by sibling consumers thrashes on every render — bound the LRU above the visible working set
statement: Caching an expensive pure parse behind an LRU that holds exactly one entry breaks the moment two sibling components parse different inputs in the same frame: each evicts the other's entry, reference stability dies, and Object.is-based store selectors re-fire forever. Key the cache by the raw input string, size it to comfortably exceed the number of simultaneously-visible consumers, and share one frozen empty result so the miss path is also referentially stable.

title: Give a degraded result a much shorter TTL, never cache an empty one
statement: Caching a partial result from a fan-out at the normal TTL hides both the failure and its recovery for the whole window. Detect the degraded case explicitly and cache it for seconds rather than minutes, so a recovered member reappears quickly while a sustained outage is still throttled — and refuse to cache a degraded result that is empty. Make the degradation observable rather than merely handled.

title: Bound media caches by bytes, and dedupe loads through an in-flight map
statement: An entry-count cap on decoded media is not a memory bound — a few hundred full-resolution images pin gigabytes. Track accumulated bytes, evict against a byte budget, never evict the entry just inserted, and release oversized entries when their last on-screen consumer unmounts. Separately, key in-flight loads by identity so simultaneous consumers cost one decode, and export an explicit invalidation so a path reused after a delete or rename cannot serve the old bytes.

title: Mirror a running total in memory instead of re-aggregating per call
statement: A pre-flight check that re-aggregates a ledger costs time proportional to the history so far, which makes a single job quadratic in its own call count — invisible in a short test and crippling in a long run. Seed the total once from the ledger at start and advance it in process on every write, so the check on the hot path is arithmetic.

title: Cache derived parses in a WeakMap keyed on the row object
statement: List rows carrying serialised columns get re-parsed on every memo re-run. Key the derived fields on the row object itself: identity is stable across re-renders and the entry is collected when a refresh replaces the row, so no eviction policy is needed. Split the cache into cheap fields computed eagerly and expensive blobs filled only on expand, with a distinct not-yet-parsed sentinel so a lazy slot is distinguishable from a real empty result.

title: Dedupe reads at two seams and hand every caller its own copy
statement: Collapse duplicate reads twice: a short in-flight window at the transport seam keyed by stably-hashed arguments, and a freshness window at the data-owner seam. Record freshness only on success so a failed fetch is never cached, evict rejections immediately so callers can retry, and deep-copy every value handed out — including to the first caller, who will otherwise mutate the cached instance in place for everyone.

title: Seed unmounting panels from a module-scoped cache of the last fetch
statement: A panel whose data lives in local component state starts genuinely cold on every remount, so a lazy route re-ghosts every time the user returns to it. Stash the last successful fetch at module scope keyed by the entity, seed state from it, and still run the fetch to replace it silently — the skeleton then appears only on a true first-ever visit. Invalidate on the mutation that changes the numbers.

title: Offload blocking database work, and re-raise the panic it swallows
statement: Calling a synchronous repository from an async task occupies a runtime worker for the whole query, starving unrelated work under pool contention. Move those bodies onto the blocking pool — and re-propagate a panic from the offloaded closure onto the awaiting future, or the move silently downgrades every panic in it from a surfaced crash with backoff to an ignored join error.

title: Give list views their own column projection
statement: When one table serves both a list and a detail view, the list pays to read, serialise and hold every heavy blob for rows the user never opens. Define a named projection for the list columns and blank the heavy fields, letting the detail fetch rehydrate them on open. Writing down which consumers read which fields is what makes the projection safe — and what tells the next person which fields must stay.

title: Use the point lookup you already have, and read shared docs once
statement: Hot request paths accumulate two quiet costs: the same record fetched twice by two independent call chains, and a list-then-find where a keyed lookup already exists and is already tested. Neither shows up in correctness tests, and both scale with tenant size rather than with traffic. Audit hot handlers for repeated reads and collection scans, and memoise per-request reads at the seam rather than at each caller.

title: Aggregate feeds with one refcounted subscription, not N hidden ones
statement: Mounting a hidden data component per entity to aggregate feeds multiplies the poll interval and the event listener by the entity count. Replace it with a shared store slice that takes refcounted declarations of interest and returns the merged result. Keep the remaining consumers named, so the merged view's bounds can be justified against real use rather than defended in the abstract.

title: Batch high-frequency discovery writes behind a buffer, and flush on every exit path
statement: Buffer mDNS events in a map keyed by peer_id and flush every 3s in one transaction (single fsync) — AND flush on both loop exits (cancellation and channel close). Use `std::mem::take` to release the lock before I/O, manual BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, and a 30s TTL trusted-peer cache to avoid per-event DB queries.

title: Gate an expensive fetch on the render branch that actually consumes it
statement: Only fire an expensive fetch when the render branch that consumes its result is active (e.g. score-trends only feeds the desktop DataGrid, so gate on pageTab==='personas' && !isMobile). Lazy-mount side panels whose eager fetch cluster was measured as wasted IPC.

title: Offload blocking probes and walks off the IPC thread
statement: A sync ~2s HTTP probe froze the webview on every poll; run blocking probes and filesystem walks in spawn_blocking, never on the IPC thread.

title: Replace an N-by-3 IPC fan-out with one aggregate command
statement: 3N invokes collapsed to 1 aggregate command; bulk settings reads the same way — each invoke costs ~1-5ms of serialisation, so fan-outs multiply invisible latency.

title: Coalesce, then debounce, then match — prune the debounce map under the same lock
statement: FS bursts: coalesce by normalized path (O(burst×triggers)→O(unique×triggers)), keep a 500ms last_fired map pruned under the same lock, release the mutex during CPU-bound matching, and count overflow in an AtomicU64 reported once per tick.

title: Tap audio once with a shared analyser, rAF-only delivery, and an idle-stop loop
statement: Audio level monitoring uses a single shared analyser tap with rAF-only imperative delivery — never 60fps through React state. attachPlayback never throws (skip the tap on failure); the rAF loop runs only while activeCount>0, decays, emits a final 0, and stops; a WeakSet tracks connected elements because an element can only be captured by one graph. The volume store stays subscribed for the LIFE of the clip so the slider works mid-sentence, unsubscribed on ended/pause/error.

title: Memoise a hook's return because a named downstream memo depends on it
statement: Memoise a hook's return value when a NAMED downstream memo depends on its identity, documenting each memo with the consumer it protects, and test the whole prop chain with the render-cost harness.

title: Precompute pair features once and prune O(n²) comparisons with best-case bounds
statement: In an all-pairs similarity scan, compute per-item features (token sets, bigram sets) once up front, drive multiple metrics from a single intersection pass, and skip the expensive metric whenever even its perfect score could not cross the decision threshold.

title: Drive N springs from one module rAF engine that writes to DOM refs
statement: Instead of N independent framer-motion springs each firing setState at 60fps, register every animated number with one module-scoped rAF loop that integrates spring physics and writes straight to the DOM via a callback — zero React reconciliation per frame. Cap dt (~64ms) so a background-tab return doesn't produce a huge integration jump, and stop the loop when everything settles.

title: Cache Intl.NumberFormat instances keyed by the options you actually vary
statement: Intl.NumberFormat construction is one of the most expensive stdlib constructors (locale resolution + option validation) and formatters run on hot paths (per-rAF counters, dozens of table cells per pass). Instances are immutable and reusable — cache them in a module Map keyed by locale + the handful of option fields you vary; the cache is naturally bounded.

title: Apply CSS containment to every table row
statement: Stamp `contain: 'layout paint style'` on each row of long lists and tables so layout and paint invalidation from an in-row change never escapes the row — cheap insurance that keeps virtualized and animated lists smooth.

title: No backdrop-blur on sticky headers — the compositor re-samples it into a flicker
statement: `backdrop-filter` re-samples its backdrop on every compositor frame, and hover/pointer repaints generate those frames — so in WebView2 a frosted sticky header flickers as a blinking white band across every module header. Use a solid/semi-transparent background on sticky chrome instead; the lesson had to be learned twice (page background, then header) so it's recorded at both sites.

title: Defer heavy subtrees behind a priority ladder with a synchronous test escape hatch
statement: Wrap expensive non-critical subtrees in a defer component with a small priority ladder — `idle` (requestIdleCallback + timeout), `next-frame` (rAF), `mount-after` (setTimeout) — with a setTimeout(0) fallback where rIC is absent, and an `immediate` prop that renders synchronously so RTL/snapshot tests stay deterministic. Motivated by the webview hanging on large single React commits.

title: Replace JSON.stringify cache-hit tests with exhaustive field comparators that short-circuit
statement: A per-item render cache over pure-rebuild derived objects cannot compare by identity — but comparing by JSON.stringify allocates a multi-kilobyte string per item, never bails early, and runs once per animation frame during hydration. Write a hand-rolled comparator that walks the same fields, short-circuits on first mismatch, and allocates nothing. Accept and DOCUMENT the one maintenance cost: a new field must be added to the comparator or changes in it paint stale.

title: Render-free gesture navigation: drive the transform imperatively, commit state on release
statement: For pan/zoom over a large scene, do not route every pointer frame through React state. Pan writes the world transform imperatively via a ref (zero re-renders), commits state exactly once on release, plus periodic mid-gesture commits every N world units so viewport culling follows the camera. Wheel zoom coalesces bursts into ≤1 state commit per animation frame (multiply accumulated factors, keep the latest pivot, flush in rAF). Guard the imperative path against unrelated re-renders: a layout effect re-asserts the live transform so React reconciliation can't snap the view back to the stale committed camera.

title: Prefer one unfiltered batch call plus client-side filtering over N scoped IPC calls
statement: When a screen needs a cross-entity rollup and the backend command only filters by a single value, one unfiltered list call filtered and grouped client-side beats multiple filtered calls — 'asking twice would double the IPC to save a client-side filter.' The same store collapses per-project fan-out (listScans × N) into one generous-limit batched list grouped client-side, invalidated surgically per project on the events that change it (scoped 20-row re-fetch merged into the cache) rather than re-polled on a timer; a single project's refresh failure logs and leaves the family status alone because 'the rest of the cache is still valid.'

title: Adapt the per-frame mount budget by measuring the previous wave instead of hardcoding it
statement: When first-mounting a heavy scene in waves (N items per animation frame), the right N is a property of the MACHINE, not the scene — a fixed constant either stalls a busy laptop or wastes frames on a workstation. Time each wave's commit and size the next wave from the result, clamped to [min, max], shrinking when commit time exceeds ~1.5 frames. Pair with viewport culling whose margin covers a whole item footprint so items are only culled once fully clear (no popping).

title: Dispatch a high-frequency stream through ONE app-wide listener into a registry map, with an eagerly-set re-entrancy flag
statement: For a per-entity output stream (PTY chunks, log lines), register exactly one app-level event listener that dispatches into a Map keyed by entity id — O(1) per chunk regardless of how many entities exist — instead of one filtered listener per entity, which makes every chunk run N callbacks. Set the singleton guard flag eagerly (before the async listen resolves) so a re-entrant call cannot double-listen, and reset it on failure so the next attach can retry.

title: Two-phase overlay open: paint the frame and cheap chrome first, mount expensive bodies a beat later
statement: When opening a surface whose tiles carry expensive mounts (canvas/WebGL/terminal attach), render the overlay frame and per-tile chrome on the first frame and gate the expensive bodies behind a short timeout state (~200ms). The switch feels instant because the layout paints immediately; the heavy cost lands after the transition instead of inside the opening render.

title: Preserve object identity across polls: compare shaped rows field-by-field and thread the previous model through the adapter
statement: A poll that re-shapes backend rows every tick produces new object identities whether or not the data moved, and identity is what the downstream memo chain keys on — an untouched surface rebuilds its whole pipeline twice a minute. Gate the setState with an allocation-free field-by-field comparison over exactly the fields the shaper writes and keep the previous array when equal; for per-row memoization, pass the previous model INTO the adapter so only genuinely-moved rows get a new reference. Pin the contract with a render-count test: one changed row costs one row render.

title: Put an explicit cell budget on quadratic diff work and degrade through a ladder of coarser algorithms
statement: An O(n*m) DP diff on user-sized inputs must check its cell count before allocating anything. Strip the common prefix/suffix first (which alone often brings the middle under budget), re-check the budget on the remainder, then fall through a graded ladder: word-level LCS, line-level LCS, and finally a whole-replaced (all-removed + all-added) rendering. Every rung still produces a correct, just coarser, result.

title: Put a debounce and a write-dedupe in front of persistent storage
statement: Persistence middleware writes synchronously on every state change, so a hot store turns a run into hundreds of blocking serialise-and-write cycles per second for a payload that mostly did not move. Wrap the storage adapter with a trailing debounce that flushes on page hide and returns the buffered value on read, and with a payload-equality check so an unchanged partialisation never reaches disk.

title: Keep frame-rate values in refs, and coalesce stream deltas per frame
statement: Anything updating at animation-frame rate — a playhead, an audio level, token deltas — must not pass through component state; a re-render per tick is the failure mode. Keep the authoritative value in a ref and let consumers subscribe and touch the DOM, buffer inbound stream deltas and flush once per frame, and force a flush before any terminal transition. Commit ref writes in a layout effect, never in the render body: a speculative render that is discarded leaves callbacks reading a thrown-away value.

title: Choose a mount policy per tab surface instead of remounting
statement: Keying a tab container on the active tab throws away and re-runs every tab's mount work on each switch. Decide deliberately instead: cheap-but-hot tabs stay mounted and are hidden, heavy tabs mount lazily and unmount after an idle timeout so memory returns while the module stays cached and re-entry is synchronous. Either way, mount only tabs the user actually visited, and validate a persisted tab id before rendering it.

title: Virtualise a table with spacer rows and an opted-in scroll parent
statement: Two traps make a virtualised table silently wrong: absolutely positioning rows breaks column alignment with the header, and resolving the scroll container by a generic overflow class can latch onto a horizontal scroller, so the offset never changes and nothing past the first viewport renders. Use zero-height spacer rows to simulate the off-screen range, require the caller to mark the vertical scroller explicitly, and keep a row-count threshold below which every row renders plainly.

title: Flatten a grouped list into one indexed sequence in a pure module
statement: A virtualiser only knows how to window a flat index range, so a two-level grouped list must be collapsed into a single ordered sequence of tagged items. Do the collapse in a pure dependency-free module so the index arithmetic is testable without a DOM, carry on each item the presentational adjacency facts the flat sequence would otherwise lose, and keep a threshold below which the plain markup renders verbatim.

title: A worker is only usable if its client handles every degenerate case
statement: Moving pure computation off the main thread is the easy half; the client around the worker is the actual pattern. Correlate requests by id, cache by content hash, stream partial results so the UI fills progressively, treat cancellation as dropping the pending entry, reject all pending work and reset the singleton on a crash so it can be lazily rebuilt, and run the same pure function inline when the worker cannot be constructed.

title: Gate new admissions on host load with asymmetric watermarks
statement: Concurrency caps tuned on an idle machine still exhaust a busy one. Sample host load on a cheap cadence and pause new admissions above a pause watermark, resuming only below a lower one so admission does not flap. Set the watermarks per metric rather than uniformly — normal idle memory pressure looks nothing like normal idle CPU — pause on any signal, resume only on all, discard the first sample, and never interrupt work already in flight.

title: Keep a long job's verbose output server-side in a bounded tail ring
statement: A chatty subprocess should cost the client nothing. Route long-running jobs through one manager owning a tail ring that keeps the most recent lines, clamps each line's size, and evicts by age and use — then give callers two sinks: one for noisy detail kept server-side and polled, one for milestones streamed to the UI. One giant line must be unable to bloat either the buffer or the payload crossing into the renderer.

title: Free decoded media with the same observer that allocated it
statement: Object URLs and media elements should be created and released by one visibility observer, so a large collection never holds more than its visible window. And any decode pipeline must tear its element down in a finally: cleanup written at the end of the success path leaks a detached element with its source still attached on every codec error or cancellation, holding the file open and its buffers resident.

title: Own expensive instances in a registry — detach is not dispose
statement: For heavyweight per-item resources like terminals, sockets or decoders, make the component a mount point and keep the instance in a module-level registry keyed by id so it survives unmount. Separate detach from dispose, bound the detached population with an eviction policy that is lossless because re-attach replays a snapshot anyway, and fan one process-wide event subscription out through the registry map — per-instance filtered listeners make every incoming chunk cost O(N).

title: Run one timer per cadence bucket, not one per poller
statement: Independent pollers start at different offsets, so a shared refresh interval becomes several desynchronised bursts and every downstream cost is paid once per ticker rather than once per window. Route them through one coordinator holding a timer per rounded cadence, guard each ticker against overlapping itself, isolate failures so one cannot poison the loop, pause while the document is hidden, and fire immediately on return.

title: Give every background poller three ways to stop
statement: A poll that reads its target id from persisted storage and swallows its errors will poll a session the backend has already collected, forever, and replay stale notifications into the next session. It needs a consecutive-failure budget that clears the stored id, an explicit clear on every terminal status, and a clear on malformed stored data — with non-terminal statuses distinguished so a resumable flow is not discarded along with the dead ones.

title: Gate polls on visibility, one owner, and the job still being alive
statement: Three independent gates make polling cost nothing when nobody is looking: skip while the document is hidden and re-run immediately on return, let exactly one always-mounted call site own the interval so the poll is not multiplied by however many components mounted, and stop entirely when the thing polled is inactive. Justify the cadence against the upstream's own refresh rate rather than picking a round number.

title: Define connection pragmas once and size the pool for real holders
statement: Two connection customisers each holding their own copy of the per-connection settings will drift, and the copy used by the less common path is the one nobody notices. Define the batch as one constant every customiser delegates to. Size the pool by the slowest realistic concurrent holder rather than a round number, set an acquire timeout so a hang becomes a recoverable error instead of a frozen UI, and log slow acquires with a caller label.

title: Actively evict per-peer caches, or a long-running daemon leaks one entry per peer
statement: `retain` the manifest hash cache against the connected set each sync round, and sweep the rate tracker with a periodic task that honors the shutdown token. Without eviction a long-running daemon leaks one entry per peer forever.

title: Spend a bounded scan budget in priority order, per-directory cap, deterministically
statement: A flat DFS spent the whole budget on one generated tree; scan in priority order with a per-directory cap and sort so the truncated set is stable — determinism matters because the scan DELETEs rows for unlisted docs.

title: Throttle a rescan to the rate the signal actually moves
statement: Skip rescans within 6h unless forced — "rot moves at commit speed, not remount speed" — and count the skips so the throttle is observable.

title: Unmount lazy tabs after an idle window instead of keeping every visited tab mounted
statement: Unmount lazy tabs after an idle window rather than keeping every visited tab mounted forever: the lazy() module stays cached so re-entry remounts synchronously, letting you shed live subscriptions and timers without paying a second network or parse cost.

title: Bound the parked-instance population with an LRU whose eviction is lossless via backend replay
statement: When detached heavyweight instances (terminals, editors, canvases) are parked for instant re-attach, keep them in an oldest-detach-first LRU with a small cap; eviction is safe only because a re-attach re-subscribes and replays the backend's bounded ring snapshot, so the recreated instance shows the same tail the parked one would have. The cap turns 'detach is not dispose' from an unbounded leak into a bounded cache.

title: Attention-tiered rendering: only entities that need the operator get the expensive live view; the rest get status blocks
statement: In a many-entity monitoring grid, define a pure predicate for 'needs the operator's eyes RIGHT NOW' and render the expensive live view (subscribed terminal, streaming pane) only for entities passing it plus the explicitly focused one; every other entity renders a cheap status block. Autonomous supervision (an agent reading backend state directly) covers the unwatched entities, so UI cost tracks attention, not fleet size.

title: Gate periodic database maintenance on a live-work gauge, not just a timer
statement: Run expensive idle maintenance (PRAGMA optimize, WAL truncate-checkpoint) on a timer, but skip the tick whenever an in-flight-work gauge shows the system is busy, so maintenance never competes with user-facing queries.

title: Set the bundle budget from measurement, in one shared constant
statement: A size budget only works when it is a single constant both the local script and CI import — a threshold passed as a CI flag is a second source of truth that drifts from what developers run — and when it is calibrated to the measured bundle rather than an aspirational round number. A threshold nobody can pass gets bypassed; one aligned to today's size catches tomorrow's regression.

title: Split localisation per route section and preload before mount
statement: One monolithic locale bundle is paid in full by every user for strings most of them never see, and loading it after mount produces a visible English first paint. Split each locale into per-section chunks at build time, declare which sections each route needs, warm the persisted locale and route before the app mounts under a bounded timeout, and expose the catalogue through a proxy that loads a section on first access so untouched sections never load at all.

title: Drain speculative imports one at a time, most likely first
statement: Scheduling many speculative imports at once does not spread their cost: resolving a chunk triggers a synchronous parse-and-evaluate that ignores the idle deadline, so they stack into one long main-thread block the moment the browser goes idle. Schedule the next only when the previous settles, delay the first past the most contended startup window, and order the queue by likelihood of use because later entries now warm noticeably later.

title: Host app-wide background hooks in one lazy render-nothing component
statement: Global side-effect hooks drag their domain stores into whatever module happens to host them, pulling that whole dependency graph into the initial bundle. Collect them in a single component that renders nothing, lazy-load it after first paint, and require each hook to carry the reason it must run app-wide rather than inside its own page — that annotation is what stops the file becoming a dumping ground.

title: Prefetch route chunks on pointer intent through one cached helper
statement: Speculative chunk loading belongs in one module where each prefetcher is memoised after its first call and a rejection resets its entry, so a failed prefetch is not permanently remembered as loaded. Fire them from real intent — pointer enter, focus, pointer down — and from idle once the landing surface has mounted. Duplicating the router's lazy imports is the one maintenance cost to accept knowingly.

title: Defer heavy below-fold subtrees behind a named priority wrapper
statement: Keeping large non-critical trees out of the first commit usually happens as a one-off timeout buried in a layout, which is untestable and gets copied without its reasoning. Make it a small wrapper that renders children at a named priority — idle, next frame, immediate — falls back to a macrotask where the idle callback is missing, and exposes a synchronous escape hatch so tests and snapshots stay deterministic.

title: Lazy-mount monitoring surfaces and pause them when nobody looks
statement: Charts, heatmaps and fleet-wide digests cost real main-thread time on a tab whose whole purpose is glanceability. Mount charts only as they approach the viewport, kick first loads at idle priority so navigating in never blocks, and make any auto-refresh stop while the document is hidden and refetch immediately on return — a stale all-green during a real outage is a status page's worst possible failure.

title: Publish an aggregate in phases, each frame complete and honest
statement: When one source in an aggregate is far slower than the rest, letting it gate first paint makes the whole surface as slow as its worst input. Publish a sequence of self-consistent frames as sources resolve, with the slower fields falling back to their documented heuristic rather than rendering blank. Guard the degraded early frame so it only paints when nothing real is on screen — painting it over cached data is a regression, not progress.
